root.name: Danish Gambit Accepted: Copenhagen Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. c3 dxc3 4. Bc4 cxb2 5. Bxb2 Bb4+

overview: White has offered two pawns with 3.c3 and 4.Bc4 and has taken back one with Bxb2; Black replies with the Copenhagen ...Bb4+ idea to return material and neutralise the attack. White has two bishops aimed at b7 and f7, a lead in development and open lines.

white_ideas.idea: Use the bishop pair on b2/c4 for pressure on b7 and f7
Develop quickly with Nc3, Nf3 and castle
Open the e-file against the Black king

black_ideas.idea: Trade the dangerous bishops with ...Bb4+ and ...Qf6
Return the extra pawns to neutralise the attack

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White missing b- and c-pawns
Bishops pointed at the Black kingside

character.notes: Open, tactical play in which Black must find the right trade.

gambit.notes: White gives two pawns and Black can keep material if careful.

soundness.notes: A strong player's verdict is that Black can equalise; the gambit is unsound but playable.

structure.notes: Central pawns are gone, so lines are open.

approach.notes: Played at club level mainly; strong players seldom choose it.

level.notes: Needs memorising the main attacks and Black's defensive tries.

soundness.reason: Black can equalise or better with accurate play.

level.reason: Not Beginner for a dubious gambit.

plans.reason: White plays for quick development and the bishops.
